Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

optimizers7 0.20.0

  • The argument ncores of multistart() is cores, and resolve_ncores() is resolve_cores(). The name is the one used by every function of the toolkit that starts separate R processes; threads counts threads inside one process.

optimizers7 0.19.0

  • Renamed for readability: the argument he of minimize(), maximize() and as_objective() is hess, and so is the element of the objective and of the test_problems() entries; curv_tol of bfgs(), lbfgs() and bb() is curvature_tol; typical of newton() and chebyshev() is typical_size; n_eps and visiting of sa() are stationarity_levels and proposal; m_serious of bundle() is accept_fraction; opportunistic of compass() is first_improvement; the elements d1 and d2 of bounded_transform() are deriv1 and deriv2.

optimizers7 0.18.0

  • gd(), cg(), bb(), bfgs() and lbfgs() take stop_decrement (default 1e-3), the last argument of each. A stopping rule on the change in the parameters or in the objective, such as crit_abs_par() or crit_abs_obj(), no longer ends a run as converged where the decrease |g’dx| / 2 that the last step still predicts at the new point exceeds stop_decrement: the run ends as not converged, with the reason in the message and the safeguard change stop refused in the trace. The check uses quantities that the loop already holds. stop_decrement = Inf restores the earlier behavior. A run that ends on the gradient rule is unchanged. bfgs() and lbfgs() from the start of a joint beta filter on Seatbelts ended at -171.51 with converged = TRUE, 0.02 of predicted decrease still left; they now end as not converged. Over 1032 gas() fits of the statmodels7 battery with bfgs() as the inner optimizer, the rule refuses 8 intermediate runs and changes no flag and no point.

optimizers7 0.17.0

  • newton() and chebyshev() take stop_decrement (default 1e-3). A stopping rule on the change in the parameters or in the objective, such as crit_abs_par() or crit_abs_obj(), no longer ends a run as converged at a point where the Hessian is not positive definite or where the Newton decrement exceeds stop_decrement: the run ends as not converged, with the reason in the message and the safeguard change stop refused in the trace. The check costs one Hessian evaluation at the point where such a stop would end the run. stop_decrement = Inf restores the earlier behavior. A run that ends on the gradient rule is unchanged.

optimizers7 0.16.0

  • newton() and chebyshev() take modify = modify_eigen(floor = 1e-8) or modify_ridge(floor = 1e-8) in place of hessian_mod and floor. The generic hessian_modify() lets a subclass of hessian_modification define another repair of an indefinite Hessian. The results of both existing repairs are unchanged.

optimizers7 0.15.2

  • The package description no longer gives a wrong count of methods (it said twelve; there are fourteen) and no longer says that every method accepts box constraints: the proximal gradient rejects them.

optimizers7 0.15.1

  • Documentation and messages: relative clauses without a relative pronoun, stranded prepositions, absolute constructions, sentences without a verb (example captions included), emphasis in bold and personified descriptions of the code rewritten as plain clauses. Messages reworded: test_problems() for an unknown name (“There is no test problem named …”), the bracketing failure of brent() (“the bracketing phase found no minimum …”), the length search of the starters (“every length … failed to give a single finite value …”), and the errors of check_criterion(), prox_grad(), plot() of a result and the starters. The label of check 10 of check_optimizer() reads “a rule that cannot be evaluated is rejected”. No change to the algorithms.

optimizers7 0.15.0

Repairs

  • In the methods with a line search (newton(), chebyshev(), bfgs(), lbfgs(), gd(), cg(), bb()), an accepted step that moves the iterate by no more than 4 * eps * max(1, max(abs(x))) is treated as a line search that found no acceptable step: the stopping rule is evaluated without the previous iterate, and otherwise the run stops with converged = FALSE, the message the step did not move the iterate beyond rounding and the safeguard step below rounding. In the same methods, when the stopping rule is met on a step dx with abs(sum(g * dx)) > max(1, abs(f)) at the new point, the step is undone and handled in the same way, with the message the step that met the stopping rule is not resolved by the objective and the safeguard step not resolved. Where the objective is rounding noise, such steps passed the Armijo condition when the noise went down, and crit_abs_par() or crit_abs_obj() then reported convergence at a gradient of order 1e27 (the exploded score filter of a beta share fitted by statmodels7, where the flag differed between platforms at the same point: 30 to 34 of 200 perturbed starts converged, none now).

optimizers7 0.14.0

Repairs

  • brent() reports its own stop under its own label. When the bracket has shrunk to the resolution of the iterate, the run ends with converged = TRUE and criterion_met equal to bracket at machine resolution; it previously reported the label of the stopping rule, even for crit_never(). The state passed to the rule now has iter and x_old, so crit_abs_par() and crit_rel_par() can fire. When max_expand expansions or the evaluation budget end the bracketing phase before a minimum is bracketed, the run stops at the lowest point evaluated with converged = FALSE and a message; it previously reduced a bracket that contained no minimum and reported convergence (9.47 on (x - 1000)^2 with max_expand = 3).
  • prox_grad() counts the evaluations of a differenced gradient in counts and in max_eval (54 reported against 446 calls before). The trace has the columns iteration, value, gnorm, step and safeguard, the last recording step shortened and momentum restart, so summary() counts them. The state passed to the rule has iter. With accelerate = FALSE the reported gradient is the proximal gradient mapping at the reported point; it was the mapping at the previous iterate. The gradient read at the iterate is reused when the next step starts there, so the plain method evaluates one gradient per iteration.
  • adam() tests its stopping rule at the point produced by the last iteration of the budget. A run with maxit equal to the iteration at which the rule holds now reports converged = TRUE, as a run with a larger budget does.
  • nelder_mead() rebuilds a degenerate simplex with edges equal to the size that it had reached. The edges were multiplied again by the size of the coordinates, so a simplex far from the origin was rebuilt about |x| times too large.
  • bundle() stores the aggregate linearization at the stability center at which it was formed. On a serious step followed by a compression it was stored at the new center, where it can lie above the objective: with bundle_size = 2 the sphere stopped at 0.044 reporting convergence. On the test problems, with bundle_size between 2 and 20, the repaired method converges on three runs that failed before and fails on two that converged.
  • maximize() negates the third-derivative contraction t3 of chebyshev(), as it negates gr and he.
  • multistart() answers optimizer_bounded() with the answer of its inner optimizer, so a multistart over prox_grad() no longer accepts bounds that the inner runs reject. with_trace() has a method for chain() that switches on the trace of every stage.
  • The counts are checked to be finite: lbfgs(memory = Inf), which ended the R session, bfgs(max_skip = Inf), armijo(max_step = Inf), nonmonotone(memory = Inf), sa(cycles = Inf), bundle(bundle_size = Inf) and multistart(ncores = Inf) are rejected.
  • The error for an invalid tolerance names the argument that was supplied ('spread', 'alpha0', …) and not 'tol'.
  • format_elapsed() chooses the unit after rounding, so that it no longer prints 59 min 60 s or 1 h 60 min.
  • The analytic Hessian of the beale test problem is finite at y = 0.
  • The message of a multistart whose first start failed no longer ends the quoted error with two periods, and the error raised when every start fails reads The first error was:.
  • The warning of newton() for a small evaluation budget states the cost as 4*p^2 + 2*p, the quantity that it computes.

Documentation

  • The documentation, the README, the vignette and the reference index were rewritten in a plain register, and claims that the code contradicted were corrected. Among them: chebyshev() reads the Hessian and shares the default rule of the gradient methods; brent() provides "stationarity"; the size of the Nelder-Mead simplex is the largest distance from the best vertex; the Corana measure of sa() and the cost of its temperature calibration (max(10, 10 * p) evaluations); the floor of newton() and the initial poll size of compass(); the trace labels of cg() and bb(); the conditions under which converged is TRUE; the seeds that a result records; the condition numbers of rosenbrock and beale (2508 and 162).

optimizers7 0.13.0

  • Every problem of test_problems() carries its analytic Hessian as he, and check_optimizer() passes it to the method under test. A method that requires a Hessian could not be checked before, since the battery supplied only the objective and the gradient.

optimizers7 0.12.1

  • The check that a supplied gradient belongs to the objective repeats its directional difference at steps ten and a hundred times smaller before it warns, and warns only if the disagreement persists. The step is scaled by the length of the starting vector, so a large coordinate made it too long for a strongly curved direction: every gas() fit in statmodels7 gave the warning (a difference of -0.00106 against an exact 0.00074 on the Nile flows), with a gradient that agrees with numDeriv to seven digits.

optimizers7 0.12.0

  • brent(), Brent’s method for a function of one variable: the minimum is bracketed by golden expansion from the starting value and the bracket is reduced by parabolic interpolation, with a golden-section step wherever the parabola is not trusted. The stationarity measure is the half-width of the bracket, so crit_stationary() reads a tolerance on the scale of the parameter. Bounds are removed by reparametrization, as in the other methods. On (x - 2)^2 + exp(-x) from 0 it takes 12 evaluations against the 42 of nelder_mead(), and it rejects a starting value of more than one coordinate.

optimizers7 0.11.0

  • chebyshev(), Newton’s method with Chebyshev’s third-order correction. Where the Hessian is positive definite the Newton step is corrected by the third derivative of the objective contracted twice with it, d = dN - H^-1 T[dN, dN] / 2, read from t3(x, d) passed to minimize(), or from one second difference of the gradient along dN without it. A correction longer than ratio times the Newton step, or one that is not a descent direction, is rejected and the Newton step kept; the rest is as in newton(). On Rosenbrock the method takes 18, 4 and 5 iterations against the 21, 14 and 8 of newton() from three starts. A t3 together with lower or upper is rejected, since the run is then on the unconstrained scale.

optimizers7 0.10.0

  • newton() takes typical, the typical size of each parameter (the scaled norm of Dennis and Schnabel). Every length used by the method is then measured in these units, the largest |d_i| / t_i in place of the largest |d_i|: the bound max_length, the length-one scaling of a direction whose Hessian was repaired, and the scaling of a gradient fallback. NULL, the default, measures them in the units of the parameters, and a run that does not set it is unchanged, which a test checks on Rosenbrock to the evaluation counts. On a restricted likelihood in a variance near 236, started at 651 where it is not concave, the repaired steps had moved the variance by one unit per iteration.

optimizers7 0.9.0

  • newton() takes max_length, the largest component that a step may have. A direction longer than this in the infinity norm is scaled down to this length before the line search, and the trace records the step as newton step capped. The default is Inf, which leaves every step as it is, so a run that does not set the argument is the run of the previous release.

    The bound is the maxstep of the line-search Newton method of Dennis and Schnabel (1983) and the maxNstep of the smoothing-parameter iteration of mgcv. Where the objective flattens towards an asymptote the curvature is small and the Newton step long, so the step can carry the iterate past the minimum into the flat region, where the line search accepts it and the gradient is close to zero. On the REML criterion of statmodels7 for a ridge penalty on the fifteen standardized predictors of MASS::UScrime, the first step from lambda = 1 had a length of 23.5 on the log scale and reached lambda = 1.6e10, where the criterion is flat at -65.40, while its maximum, -53.30, lies near lambda = 91.5. With max_length = 5 the same search reaches the maximum.

    Near a minimum the Newton steps are short and the bound does not bind, so the quadratic convergence of the method is kept. On Rosenbrock from the customary start a bound of 10 leaves the run identical to the unbounded one, to the evaluation counts. On sqrt(1 + x^2), whose Newton step from 2 is -10, a bound of 1 takes every step at full length and needs fewer evaluations than the unbounded method, which backtracks its first step.

optimizers7 0.8.0

  • The adaptive restart of prox_grad() compares an increase in the objective with an allowance for its rounding error, eight units in the last place of the current objective, and not with zero. The objective is a sum, so its error grows with the number of terms, and a bare > test fires on that error near the solution, discarding the momentum at each spurious reset.

    On the lasso of the prox_grad() page (200 observations, eight coefficients, three non-zero in the truth) at crit_grad(1e-9) the run took 21646 iterations before and 782 after, at the same support and the same objective. At the default crit_grad(1e-6) both take 11. Allowances between one and thirty-two units gave the same run, and 256 units cost iterations on an ill-conditioned problem by suppressing real restarts. On a smooth quadratic in eight unknowns at crit_grad(1e-8) the allowance changes the iteration counts of the restarted method from 149, 571 and 934 to 150, 573 and 1042 at condition numbers 55, 480 and 2400.

    restart = FALSE is unchanged: 89 iterations on the same lasso.

optimizers7 0.7.0

  • The abstract starter class is exported. A stopping rule inherits from criterion() and an algorithm from optimizer(), both exported, while a starting-value generator had to inherit from an internal class: starting_values() was exported, but minimize() rejected the resulting object with 'par' must be a numeric vector of starting values, since it tests inheritance from the class. A user-defined starter now runs as the two shipped ones do. Existing calls are unchanged.

  • bfgs() and lbfgs() validate curv_tol, and bfgs() validates max_skip; both were accepted at any value. curv_tol multiplies |s||y| in the test of the curvature of a secant pair, so a negative value weakens the protection (bfgs(curv_tol = -1) ran identically to the default on Rosenbrock, the protection never firing). max_skip is compared with >=, so a negative value behaves as zero (max_skip = -3, 0 and 5 gave the same 500 iterations when the skip path was forced). Zero is admitted for both: curv_tol = 0 is the textbook condition s'y > 0, and max_skip = 0 resets the approximation on the first skipped update.

  • check_count() rejects a fractional value, as its page stated. As a consequence lbfgs(memory = 2.5) is rejected instead of running at a memory of 2, and armijo(max_step = 2.5), wolfe(max_step = 2.5) and nonmonotone(max_step = 2.5) are rejected, as the example of armijo() showed.

  • check_whole() and check_nonneg() validate a count that may be zero and a threshold that may not be negative. nonmonotone() calls the first in place of its inline check, with the same message and bounds.

optimizers7 0.6.0

  • The six gradient methods gd(), cg(), bb(), newton(), bfgs() and lbfgs() default to crit_any(crit_grad(), crit_abs_obj(), crit_abs_par()) instead of crit_any(crit_grad(), crit_rel_obj()). A disjunction only becomes weaker as terms are added, so a run that stops under the new rule would not have stopped earlier under the old one. Over test_problems(), six methods on eight problems, 44 of 48 runs converge instead of 41, at 19370 evaluations of the objective and the gradient instead of 22299. The three runs gained are cg and bb on the non-smooth abs_sum and gd on Beale; none is lost.

    A run stops sooner and reports a point further from the solution. Ten of the 48 end at a gradient more than a hundred times larger: bfgs on Rosenbrock ends at 8.1e-06 instead of 4.4e-10, the objective 3.2e-13 above its minimum instead of 1.2e-21. One run differs in substance: cg on abs_sum ends 4.5e-02 above the minimum instead of 1.9e-03 and now reports convergence, since on a non-smooth problem a smooth method stalls far from the solution and a rule that reads a stall reports it as convergence. criterion = crit_grad() restores the previous behavior.

  • crit_rel_obj() leaves the default rule, since it never fired in it: over the same 48 runs the rule with it and the rule without it agree on every convergence flag, every evaluation count and every reported point. It remains exported.

optimizers7 0.5.0

  • newton() multiplies a direction computed from a repaired Hessian by min(1, 1/||d||_inf), which gives a displacement of order one in the parameters. Where the Cholesky factorization succeeds the direction is unchanged, since it is the Newton step and its length is set by the curvature. Where it fails, the component in the floored subspace is g_i / (floor * max|lambda|), whose size comes from floor and not from the curvature, so step = 1 is not a Newton unit there. The rule is the one that bb() applies when its secant pair has no usable curvature and that bfgs() and lbfgs() apply to their first direction, and it never lengthens a step.

  • The same scaling applies to the gradient direction that newton() uses when the Hessian is not finite or a solve fails.

  • The trace reports a scaled step as "hessian modified (capped)", and "hessian modified" where the direction was already of order one.

  • On the indefinite-Hessian test of the package the first component of the repaired direction was 5.03e+06, bounded only by the line search: the saddle cost 28 evaluations before and 5 after with hessian_mod = "eigen", 30 and 5 with "ridge". Over test_problems() under newton(), 743 evaluations became 480 and 8 of 8 problems converged instead of 7 (abs_sum went from 180 evaluations and a gradient of 1.0 to 27 evaluations and a gradient of exactly 0). The four problems on which the scaling never applies (sphere, rosenbrock, booth, powell) are unchanged to the evaluation counts.

optimizers7 0.4.0

  • armijo(), wolfe() and nonmonotone() take a resolution: the smallest difference in the objective that the objective can resolve, in its own units. It defaults to 0, which disables the test, so a caller who does not set it sees no change.

  • It may be a function of no arguments instead of a number, for an objective whose resolution changes during the run (a fit warm-started from the previous evaluation becomes more precise at each one, so the value measured at the start is the worst of the run; on a penalized smooth it was 14 to 22 times the best later one). The function is called once per invocation of the search, so it costs one call per iteration, and a value that is not finite and positive is read as 0.

  • It is for an objective computed by a procedure (a warm-started fit, a quadrature whose panels move, a simulation), which returns slightly different values for the same argument. Differences below that spread carry no information, and a search that keeps backtracking uses its whole budget: on a marginal likelihood whose coefficients are refitted at every evaluation, 30 evaluations, the backtracking budget, each a complete inner fit.

  • The test is made once, on the full step, and not inside the backtracking loop. The quantity is the decrease predicted by the linear model of the method, alpha0 * |g'd|, and when it is below the resolution the search returns at once: the point is optimal to the accuracy of the objective, and the result reports no decrease above the objective's resolution instead of a stopping rule being met.

  • Inside the loop the test is unsafe, because the two situations cannot be distinguished as the step shrinks: x + alpha d tends to x whether the point is optimal or the direction is wrong, and an incorrect gradient at a point far from stationarity was reported as convergence. At the full step they differ, since a wrong direction predicts a large decrease and the search reports a failure. The tests cover both cases.

  • The quantity is the predicted decrease and not the Armijo threshold c1 * alpha0 * |g'd|, which at the default c1 = 1e-4 is four orders of magnitude smaller and would fire while the method can still make progress.

optimizers7 0.3.0

  • bfgs() and lbfgs() scale their first direction to a step of order one in the parameters. A quasi-Newton direction is scaled so that step = 1 is the Newton step, which is why both default to it; on the first iteration, and after a reset, there is no curvature information and the direction is -g, for which one is not a natural unit. The trial displacement is then the gradient itself, so on a badly scaled objective the first point tried is at an arbitrary distance and the line search backtracks.

    The rule is the one that bb() uses when its secant pair has no curvature: 1/||g||_inf cannot freeze, since it does not depend on the step that it replaces, and cannot explode, since it scales with the gradient. The factor min(1, 1/||g||_inf) never lengthens a step, so a problem whose gradient at the start is of order one takes the same path.

    gd() and cg() are unchanged: there the direction is the gradient by design and the step length is the task of the line search.

    On test_problems(), before against after: the same 14 of 16 converged, total evaluations 984 to 883, and the gradient at the reported solution equal or smaller on every problem (rosenbrock under bfgs, 1.15e-07 to 4.37e-10). Per problem, rosenbrock 108 to 90, booth 26 to 16, powell 112 to 84. On 0.5*1e4*|x|^2 from x0 = 1, 19 evaluations became 4. On the marginal criterion of statmodels7 over a score-driven panel, four panels that needed a derivative-free search, or failed, fit in 5 to 8 criterion evaluations against 23 to 55.

optimizers7 0.2.0

  • sa(), simulated annealing with an adaptive step. The parameters move one coordinate at a time and the step of each coordinate is adjusted every few sweeps to hold its acceptance rate near a target (Corana et al. 1987), which makes the method usable on a statistical objective, whose unconstrained coordinates lie on scales orders of magnitude apart. The proposal is uniform or Cauchy, the second being the visiting distribution of fast simulated annealing (Szu and Hartley 1987), the q = 2 member of the Tsallis family; the general Tsallis visiting distribution is not implemented. The initial temperature is calibrated from the variation of the objective unless the caller sets it, so the same problem scaled by a million is solved as well. The run returns the best point seen and not the last, and converged is not inferred from the end of the schedule: the stationarity measure is Corana’s termination rule, read by crit_stationary(). sa_run_r() is an R twin of the compiled loop; the two draw from the generator of R in the same order, so from one seed they give the same run and the test needs no tolerance. The compiled loop is 1.74 times faster on an objective costing 0.7 microseconds and 1.34 times on one costing 3.8; on an objective of half a millisecond, the cost of an inner fit of a modeling layer, the loop overhead is a quarter of a per cent.

  • chain(), which runs optimizers one after another, each starting where the previous one finished: chain(sa(), lbfgs()) explores and then descends, and neither method needs code for the other. It is the second wrapper after multistart(), and the two combine. Each stage carries its own criterion and budgets; the point, the value and converged are those of the last stage, the work is summed, and the trace has a stage column.

  • The ninth check of check_optimizer() runs its maximize() comparison from the same random stream as the minimize() run that it is compared with, as the eighth check already did. Without it the check required the optimizer to converge tightly enough that two independent runs agree to 1e-5, which the mesh-shrinking methods do, so it passed for the wrong reason on them and failed on a global search.

optimizers7 0.1.0

Methods

  • prox_grad(), the proximal gradient method: an accelerated iteration with backtracking and adaptive restart. Its loop is written in R, every iteration calling a proximal operator supplied by the caller. On one seeded lasso draw acceleration mattered on ill-conditioned problems only: at a condition number of 3 the plain iteration was slightly faster, at 55 it took 4153 iterations against 126, and at 480 it did not converge in 50000 while the accelerated one took 334.

  • optimizer_bounded() declares whether a method accepts box bounds beside the objective. It is FALSE for prox_grad(), which takes its constraint inside the operator; check_optimizer() reads it before testing bounds.

  • nonmonotone(), a third line_search subclass implementing the condition of Grippo, Lampariello and Lucidi, and the default for bb(). With memory = 0 it is armijo() value for value. With the default memory on Rosenbrock, bb() took 68 iterations and 77 evaluations against 82 and 186 under armijo(), accepting eleven uphill steps out of sixty-seven, where Armijo accepts none.

  • bb() takes its fallback step from 1/max|g| when the secant pair has no usable curvature. Freezing the previous step length traps a short step (873 of 945 iterations, on bb2), and restarting at alpha0 does the same wherever alpha0 is too short (1395 rejected steps in 1521 iterations, on a boxed quadratic). alpha_max, which the SPG literature uses, gives the search a direction of length 1e10, and the run stopped a unit from the solution reporting convergence. The curvature test is relative, s'y > curv_tol*||s||*||y||, as in bfgs().

  • start_zeros() and start_runif(), so that a starting value need not be written out, and multistart() runs its starts in parallel by default.

Stopping and reporting

  • The default gradient tolerance is 1e-6, in crit_grad() and in every method that uses it. A line search accepts a step only when the objective decreases by a definite amount, so the smallest gradient that a run can reach is about sqrt(2*lambda*eps*|f*|), which grows with the value at the solution. Every problem in test_problems() has f* = 0, where that floor is zero; a log-likelihood divided by the number of observations is of order one at its maximum, and the floor is then around 1e-8. Across families, methods and seeds it reached 1.06e-8.

  • gd(), cg(), bb(), newton(), bfgs() and lbfgs() no longer restate the tolerances in their defaults, so a change to crit_grad() reaches them.

  • A run evaluates its stopping rule before reporting a line-search failure. A search that found no acceptable step ended the loop with converged = FALSE even when the start was already the answer, as it is for a caller who passes a closed-form estimate. The rule is evaluated without a previous value, so a rule on a change of the objective returns FALSE and only the state at the point can end the run.

  • The gradient check is skipped at a stationary start. Differencing the objective along a direction without slope gives the truncation error of the difference, so the check warned exactly when the caller supplied the optimum.

  • A supplied gradient is checked once against the objective, with one central difference along the gradient direction at par, and a large disagreement gives a warning that names both rates. Disable it with options(optimizers7.check_gradient = FALSE).

  • newton() without gr and he warns when the evaluation budget admits fewer than two iterations, and max_eval defaults to Inf.

Interface

  • Box constraints are two vectors, lower and upper, instead of a list of pairs, so lower = 0 makes every parameter positive.

  • adam(resample = ) and finite_sum() are removed. An objective that draws its own minibatches is a closure written in one line, and the two required a second objective class, a rule for the criteria that they permitted, a name in the criterion machinery, a branch in the compiled loop and an argument to select the path.

  • cpp_objective() is removed. The pointer type double(*)(const arma::vec&) has no closure, so a statistical objective needed C++ globals, which is not reentrant.

  • multistart() runs its starts sequentially under pkgload. Its PSOCK workers load the installed copy of the package, so an S7 optimizer built in a development namespace dispatched against the methods of the installed namespace and the inner runs returned wrong results without an error.

Validation and documentation

  • check_optimizer() separates what an optimizer reports from its performance: twelve checks on what it reports (that value is the objective at par, that converged follows the rule and is not inferred from the end of the run, that bounds hold strictly, and others), followed by a battery of standard problems whose gaps are printed as information. It found two defects in bundle(), one of them a stationarity measure that contained the trust parameter, which the algorithm shrinks for reasons of its own.

  • check_bounds(), check_criterion() and as_objective() are exported, because a user-defined optimizer cannot honor box constraints or reject a stopping rule that it cannot evaluate without them.

  • Every constructor cites the paper of its method, every exported topic carries a \value and an executable example, and the class pages live at X-class with the plain name as an alias, since two topics that differ only in case are one file on Windows.

  • A vignette on extending the package, a README with badges, a pkgdown site and continuous integration on five platforms.
